bib.title: Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents

read.skipped: reference list skimmed; sample plans in A.5 skimmed

question: Can world knowledge in pre-trained LLMs be used, without further training, to produce executable action plans for high-level tasks in an embodied environment?
hypothesis: Large enough LMs prompted appropriately can decompose high-level tasks into mid-level plans, and plans can be made executable by translating to admissible actions.
contributions: Show that without training, LLMs can generate plausible goal-driven action plans, but frequently not executable
Propose tools to improve executability without invasive probing or modification of the model
Human evaluation of multiple techniques and models, reporting the executability/correctness trade-off

method.summary: Frozen causal Planning LM is prompted with the most similar demonstration (by Sentence-RoBERTa embedding), generates k single-step samples at a time, each is mapped to the nearest admissible VirtualHome action by cosine similarity plus beta times mean log prob, and the admissible action is appended to the prompt. Evaluated by executability in VirtualHome and human-judged correctness.
method.task: Grounding high-level task names to executable VirtualHome action programs

datasets.name: ActivityPrograms (VirtualHome, Puig et al.)
datasets.split: 88 random held-out tasks for evaluation; 204 tasks as demonstration set (also used to fine-tune the baseline)
datasets.preprocessing: Detailed instructions omitted (except Sec 5.4); programs converted to natural-language templates for 42 atomic actions

models.name: Sentence-RoBERTa (large) Translation LM
models.architecture: BERT-style, Sentence-BERT objective, mean-pooled last layer

other.ablations: Sentence BERT base 110M, large 340M, Sentence RoBERTa base 125M, avg GloVe

inference.decoding: temperature sampling plus nucleus sampling; Vanilla picks the sample with highest mean log prob among k; Translated picks best admissible action per step
inference.temperature: grid {0.1, 0.3, 0.6}; chosen value per method not stated
inference.samples: k in {1,10} samples per step; one plan evaluated per task; metrics averaged over 3 randomly chosen fixed prompt examples; executability over 88 tasks x 7 scenes; correctness over 10 annotators
inference.prompting: One example task+plan prepended (fixed for Vanilla, from 3 candidates; nearest-neighbour from 204 demonstrations for Translated)
inference.retrieval: nearest demonstration by cosine similarity of Translation LM embeddings of task names

parameters.early_stop: > 50% of step samples 0-length or best score < epsilon
parameters.selection: rank runs by sum of LCS and executability, each normalised by human-expert scores

metrics.name: Executability
metrics.definition: plan parses and satisfies pre/post-conditions in VirtualHome; averaged over 88 tasks and 7 scenes

metrics.name: Correctness
metrics.definition: MTurk annotators answer Yes/No whether plan completes task; mean over 10 annotators, SEM across annotators

metrics.name: LCS
metrics.definition: longest common subsequence with human program normalised by max length, max over references

eval.protocol: Human evaluation on MTurk, shuffled and blind, 88 tasks, 10 annotators; no significance test; empirical max human-human LCS 0.489

limits: Correctness drops when executability rises (Codex 12B 64.87% to 54.88%)
Only mid-level grounding; assumes a low-level controller
No environment observation or feedback; one instance per object class
Single environment (household VirtualHome); correctness depends on its limited expressivity; human-written plans only 64-70% complete
Evaluation metric LCS is only a proxy; correctness judged by MTurk annotators; no significance tests
Small models score high executability by repeating the prompt example
Fine-tuning details of baseline not given; hyperparameter chosen per method by grid search on the same evaluation tasks
